request: Cross-test payment/refund behavior and fix discovered defects before final deployment verification
title: Serialize refund processing before payment provider calls
purpose: Prevent concurrent partial refunds from diverging between the processor and database

files.purpose: Serialize same-order refunds before external side effects.
files.previous_behavior: Concurrent different partial refund amounts could both reach the processor before a database compare-and-set rejected one, leaving totals inconsistent.
files.new_behavior: A nonblocking per-order PostgreSQL transaction lock is acquired before reading totals or invoking the processor. A busy request returns ConflictError without a second processor call; refund records, revocation and audit commit within the same bounded transaction.
files.data_impact: Updates the same Order, Enrollment, Subscription and AuditLog records as before. No schema or production-data migration.
files.access_control_impact: Existing commerce authorization is unchanged. Same-order competing refund requests now fail before provider access.
risks: The transaction holds one DB connection for the provider call, bounded by a 30-second transaction timeout and a 20-second provider request timeout.
A provider-success/database-failure outcome still needs reconciliation/retry using the existing idempotency key; live PG behavior is not proven by a synthetic test.
files.rollback: Revert this commit and rebuild apps consuming @bayada/services. Preserve all financial and audit records; reverting restores the concurrency weakness and must not be treated as a data rollback.

files.purpose: Verify payment and refund persistence with real QA transactions while completely replacing external fetch.
files.previous_behavior: No integration coverage proved simultaneous refunds kept processor and database totals aligned.
files.new_behavior: Eleven QA checks cover price validation, duplicate confirmation, request ownership, request rejection, partial/full refund access, pass cancellation, concurrency and failure/retry. Non-QA DB endpoints are refused and fetch never reaches the network.
files.data_impact: Writes synthetic QA accounts, courses, plans, orders and their access/audit records only; no production changes or real processor operations.
files.access_control_impact: Existing commerce authorization is unchanged. Same-order competing refund requests now fail before provider access.
risks: The transaction holds one DB connection for the provider call, bounded by a 30-second transaction timeout and a 20-second provider request timeout.
A provider-success/database-failure outcome still needs reconciliation/retry using the existing idempotency key; live PG behavior is not proven by a synthetic test.
files.rollback: Revert this commit and rebuild apps consuming @bayada/services. Preserve all financial and audit records; reverting restores the concurrency weakness and must not be treated as a data rollback.

production_safety.operational_data: No production payment/order/enrollment data touched. Tests wrote only to the separate synthetic QA database and intercepted every payment-provider fetch in process.
production_safety.schema_migration: None. PostgreSQL advisory transaction locks require no persistent schema objects.
external_side_effects: Zero actual payment-provider network calls; only synthetic QA database traffic. No mail or public routing changes in this patch.

verification.evidence: 11 checks passed. Before the fix, concurrent partial refunds reproduced DB total 2000 vs synthetic processor total 5000. After the fix, one request is rejected with 409 before provider access; totals agree, and retry after a simulated network failure succeeds. Evidence output/qa-payment-integration-evidence.json.

residual_risks: Application images containing this patch still need to be built, verified and deployed; currently active runtime remains 31240ce.
Live merchant payment approval/refund is not exercised; configuration and external payment outcome remain separately reported dependencies.
External merchant-dashboard cancellations or provider success followed by a DB outage need operational reconciliation beyond the concurrency regression tested here.
Broader goal verification and final report remain active.
